episodes.verdict: Ready: post it as it is. The open (face paint, empty stand, "I'M A BIT EARLY." on frame one) holds a muted stranger and every beat reads from picture and words alone (only adult in face paint / also the only adult; staff asked him to leave / it is his seat; match moved to Thursday, flight home Wednesday, stamp ARRIVED; the grandmother travels on the day). No blockers or majors; the three minors below are worth ten minutes only if the project is still open.

findings.what: His clothes change inside one unbroken shot: a navy crew-neck over a checked collar from 0 to about 6.3, then a white shirt and black tie once the sandwich comes down. The caption plate half-hides it until 13.46; after that he stares at the lens for 0.58 s with the tie in the middle of the frame and nothing else to look at.
findings.evidence: Full-size crops at 4.0 / 9.0 / 13.7 in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6c5eacab-9362-529e-a035-ffc0b493a7b7/scratchpad/final-later/e5-wardrobe.jpg. There is no cut between 0 and 14.04 (frame-change score stays under 0.08); the plate leaves at 13.46, the cut is at 14.04.
findings.fix: Hold the "He has explained that it is his seat." plate up to the cut at 14.04 so it keeps covering the collar and knot; if the tie still shows below it, push in about 8% on 10.9-14.04. Keep the stare.

findings.what: The line starts on the first frames: "I'm" begins 0.03 s into the file, where episodes 4 and 6 leave about 0.23 s. On autoplay and on the loop the first syllable is what a player swallows.
findings.evidence: 10 ms peak envelope of the mix: ambience at -27 to -36 dBFS for 30 ms, speech at -13 dBFS by 40 ms and -7 by 60 ms. Speech onset in E4 is 0.23 s, in E6 0.24 s.
findings.fix: Add 4-5 frames of picture before the line (slip the sound 0.2 s later), as in the other two.

findings.what: The sign-off stands for 1.87 s: "VENUVOY" plus "Next episode: Thursday. Confirmed." (41 characters), arriving 1.3 s after a two-line tag that is itself a joke, and the reel loops the instant it ends. The size is fine; the time is at the floor, and a stranger who lingers on the grandmother gets half the line.
findings.evidence: Text contrast measured against a mask of the last frame: 20% at 22.26, 90% at 22.38, file ends at 24.25. Identical in all three (E4 30.72-32.58, E6 19.13-21.00); end card is 3.58 s in each.
findings.fix: Give the end card 0.7-0.8 s more (run the grandmother shot at about 80% speed, not a freeze) so the sign-off stands about 2.6 s. Same change in all three.

episodes.verdict: Ready: post it as it is. The strongest of the three: the hook lands inside the first second and every beat pays (a different team won a different match so this one moved; the flight home did not and its card turns red; the counter goes up from 40 to 42; cancelled Monday on Tuesday; T-shirts say Saturday; the match moved at NO CHARGE; "Do not ask" then two people typing; his daughter's wedding, he did ask her; the grandmother is free on Monday). No blockers or majors.

findings.what: The day-counter chip sits on Vic's head for the whole of his shot, through both punchlines: its left end covers 80-100 px of his scalp at the hairline. Maya's shot in the same episode clears the same chip.
findings.evidence: Frame 25.4 at full size, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6c5eacab-9362-529e-a035-ffc0b493a7b7/scratchpad/final-later/e4-f254.png: chip at x 622-1040, y 262-338; his scalp runs to about x 720 at that height. Same at 24.2 and 28.2, and in the 4:5 file at 26.4.
findings.fix: Reframe Vic's shot only: drop the picture about 125 px (Maya's shot here already sits 127 px lower than in episode 6, which is what clears her), or push in about 8% and slide left until his head is clear of x 620 at the chip's height. Leave the chip where it is.

findings.what: After the push-in on the chat, the placeholder word "Message" in the input bar is sliced through the middle by the bottom edge of the frame for about two seconds.
findings.evidence: 4:5 frame at 23.2, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6c5eacab-9362-529e-a035-ffc0b493a7b7/scratchpad/final-later/e4-45-232.png. In the 9:16 the word is whole; in episode 6's 4:5 the bar is cropped out cleanly, leaving no cut letters.
findings.fix: In the 4:5 layout raise the zoomed chat about 60 px, or push the input bar fully out of frame as episode 6 does.

findings.what: Same as episode 5: the sign-off (brand plus "Next episode: Thursday. Confirmed.") stands for 1.87 s, 1.3 s after the "FREE ON MONDAY." tag, then the reel loops.
findings.evidence: Text contrast against a mask of the last frame: 90% at 30.72, file ends at 32.58.

episodes.verdict: Ready: post it as it is. The driest open of the three (a tired face and one flat sentence), but the line is readable for 2.1 s, the chat arrives at 2.5 s, the run "It's pinned. / where / Top of the chat. / cheers Sydney" reads without sound, and TIME: TO BE CONFIRMED is the best ending of the set (asked fourteen times under the pin; answered from Sydney at two in the morning; the pinned message has no time; the grandmother is not in the chat). No blockers or majors.

findings.what: When the chat pulls back to show the pinned message, the narrator plate "This is the pinned message." lands exactly on top of the "Message" input field, edge to edge, for 1.2 s. It reads as one stacked box at the moment the eye should be travelling up to "TIME:".
findings.evidence: Lower third of frame 15.2 at full size, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6c5eacab-9362-529e-a035-ffc0b493a7b7/scratchpad/final-later/e6-f152.png: plate bottom and field top share a line, with the plate's shadow on the field. At 14.3, before the pull-back, there is a clear gap. Same contact in the 4:5 at 15.0.
findings.fix: Sit the input field about 60 px lower in the pulled-back layout (the chat below it is empty), or raise this one plate about 30 px. The line is spoken until 15.25, so keep the plate up.

findings.what: Same as the other two: the sign-off stands for 1.87 s, 1.3 s after the "NOT IN THE CHAT." tag, then the reel loops.
findings.evidence: Text contrast against a mask of the last frame: 90% at 19.13, file ends at 21.00.
findings.fix: Give the end card 0.7-0.8 s more (grandmother shot at about 80% speed) so the sign-off stands about 2.6 s.

across: Head before the first word: E5 speaks 0.03 s into the file, E4 at 0.23 s and E6 at 0.24 s. Give E5 the same 0.2 s.

The day-counter chip against faces: it clears Maya (her E4 shot is the E6 set-up dropped 127 px at the same scale, which is why) but bites 80-100 px into Vic's scalp for his whole shot in E4. Treat Vic the way Maya was treated.
4:5 chat push-in: E4 leaves the word "Message" cut through by the bottom edge; E6 crops the input bar out cleanly. Make E4 match E6.

Name tags: Maya (ORGANISER) and Vic (HOLDS ALL SIX TICKETS) carry a role line, Lee carries a name only, and the E5 supporter has no tag at all (the board calls him ONE SUPPORTER). Fine if Lee's blank is meant; if it is an omission, give him a line.

Narrator caption position: fixed in one place everywhere except E5 at 6.2-8.7, where "He is also / the only adult present." jumps to the top of the frame and the next caption drops back down. It is motivated by the sandwich and still reads; noted only because it is the one caption in the set that moves, and it moves on the best line.

Checked and the same, nothing to fix: sign-off wording, size, position and timing (end card 3.58 s, sign-off legible for the last 1.87 s in each, so the one lengthening applies to all three); loudness (-14.1 LUFS integrated in all three, peaks about -2 dBFS, clean first and last samples); Maya's face, sweatshirt, kitchen, mug and tag in E4 and E6; chip position and type in E4 and E6, with the counter running the right way (42 then 37); the silence held after each of the three stamps (about 1.2 s); grandmother shot, tag style and clock ticks. One scheduling note: all three promise "Next episode: Thursday. Confirmed.", so each needs a Thursday post after it.
